# dsh-glass-skin
Acrylic / frosted-glass appearance for DeepSeek Harness: translucent surfaces that let **your deskto
p show through the window**, layered on top of whatever theme you already use.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
One command. It installs the plugin *and* patches the window material.

> **npm 12 and newer refuse git dependencies by default.** `npx` fails with
> `EALLOWGIT: Fetching p

ackages of type "git" have been disabled` unless the flag
> above is passed. On older npm the flag i
s unnecessary and harmless.
> **Windows 11** is the fully supported platform (native acrylic). On macOS the plugin half works an
d uses the vibrancy the app already has. On Linux the window patch is skipped.
## What you get
| Layer | Effect |

| **Native window material** | the OS blurs the desktop behind the window (acrylic on Windows) |
| *
*Glass surfaces** | the app's own backgrounds become 70–82% transparent, keeping the active theme's

colours |
| **Frosted blur** | a 30px backdrop blur so text stays readable over a busy wallpaper |
Works **together with existing theme plugins**. It does not replace your theme; it stacks on top of
it. Mineradio, the official homepage theme, open-sea-skin and custom themes all keep their palette —
only opacity changes.

## Uninstall
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or just turn it off: **Settings → General → Glass skin**. That restores your surfaces immediately an
d leaves the window patch in place (the window stays blurred acrylic).
To restore the window exactly as it shipped, `--uninstall` puts back the byte-exact backup the insta
the window exactly as it shipped, `--uninstall` puts back the byte-exact backup the installer made.
## After a DSH update
**A DSH update silently removes the window patch.** The updater replaces `resources/app.asar` wholes
ale, so the patched `lib/main.js` is gone — but the Client plugin in your profile is untouched. The
result is a confusing half-state: surfaces stay translucent, yet the desktop no longer shows through
, because nothing is asking the OS for acrylic any more.
The fix is to start the app through the launcher, which patches first and then launches:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
That writes a **DeepSeek Harness (Glass)** shortcut to your Desktop. From then on, start the app wit
h that shortcut instead of the normal icon: it applies the patch while the app is closed, then start
t shortcut instead of the normal icon: it applies the patch while the app is closed, then starts it.
[该节后续省略]
## Why a patch is needed at all
Two layers are required, and only one of them can be a pure plugin.
The **surfaces** are a plugin: DSH lets a client plugin stack a theme-token overlay via `ctx.theme.o
verrideTokens()`, which is the cooperative path — the theme service composes it on every palette swi
tch, so it survives theme changes and does not fight other themes.
The **window material** cannot be a plugin. `transparent` / `backgroundMaterial` are `BrowserWindow`
constructor options evaluated when Electron creates the window, before any plugin code runs. So the
installer makes one surgical, **length-preserving** edit to `lib/main.js` inside `app.asar`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
It inserts N bytes and removes exactly N bytes from an adjacent JSDoc comment, so the archive's size
, header and **every entry offset stay identical**. Before replacing anything it verifies: size unch
anged, header byte-identical, all entry offsets unchanged, only `lib/main.js` differs, and the extra
cted file still parses. If any check fails, nothing is written.
### Why not `transparent: true`?
Measured on Electron 44.7.0 / Windows 11 26300 over a high-frequency checkerboard backdrop:
| Window options | Desktop visible | Genuinely blurred | Native shadow |

| `backgroundMaterial:"acrylic"` | yes | **yes** | **intact** |
| `+ transparent: true` | yes | yes

| **collapses to ~2px** |
| `transparent: true` only | yes | **no** — crisp, not blurred | ~2px |
|
`backgroundMaterial:"mica"` | **no** | — | none |
`acrylic` alone already yields a real blurred backdrop *and* keeps the window shadow. Adding `transp
arent: true` costs the shadow without improving the blur. It is also the exact shape DSH's own welco
me window already uses.
### Why the blur is a separate layer
`backdrop-filter` makes an element a **containing block for fixed-position descendants**. The shell'
s menus and dialogs are viewport-positioned, so putting the filter on the app frame would silently r
e-anchor every popover to that frame — and on Windows the frame is offset by the title bar, so every
thing would shift down.
Instead the plugin appends **one empty fixed layer at `z-index:-1`**, behind all content. It has no
children, so it cannot become anyone's containing block.
## Compatibility
- **DSH 0.2.x** (Electron 44). The patch anchors on `createWindow()` in `lib/main.js`; if a future r

elease moves it, the tool **refuses and reports** instead of guessing.
- **Theme plugins**: unaffect

ed — the overlay reads colours *from* the theme registry and only changes alpha.
- **`prefers-reduce
d-transparency: reduce`**: the plugin turns itself off and says so in Settings instead of ignoring y

ou.
- **Menus and popovers** stay opaque on purpose, so they remain readable.
- **An app update repl
aces `app.asar`** and drops the window patch. Re-run the installer; your plugin and its settings sur
`app.asar`** and drops the window patch. Re-run the installer; your plugin and its settings survive.
